candidate.answerReason: The two regions are complete disks with squared radii \(49\) and \(4998\). Their defining quadratic inequalities already ensure \(x+y>0\), so the logarithm domain removes no part of either disk.

methods.label: Convert the inequalities into disks
methods.explanation:
The logarithms suggest first combining each constant with \(\log_{10}(x+y)\). The left logarithm arguments are always positive, so the only initial domain restriction is \(x+y>0\).

Because \(1=\log_{10}10\), \(2=\log_{10}100\), and the base-10 logarithm is increasing, the two inequalities are equivalent on that domain to
\[
\begin{aligned}
1+x^2+y^2&\le10(x+y),\\
2+x^2+y^2&\le100(x+y).
\end{aligned}
\]
Completing the square reveals their geometric shapes:
\[
\begin{aligned}
(x-5)^2+(y-5)^2&\le49,\\
(x-50)^2+(y-50)^2&\le4998.
\end{aligned}
\]
We must check whether the restriction \(x+y>0\) cuts either disk. Every point satisfying the first quadratic inequality has
\[
10(x+y)\ge1+x^2+y^2>0,
\]
and every point satisfying the second has \(100(x+y)\ge2+x^2+y^2>0\). Thus the restriction holds throughout both disks, including their boundaries.

Their areas are \(49\pi\) and \(4998\pi\), respectively. Hence the requested ratio is
\[
\frac{4998\pi}{49\pi}=\boxed{102},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
